item.title: Assistant Legal Counsel
item.description: Job title: Better Society Capital, Assistant Legal Counsel Location: London EC1Y/Hybrid Reporting To: General Counsel Contract: Fixed Term 12 months Salary: £55,000-£65,800 Date Closes: Thursday 13th August Role Purpose: Better Society Capital (BSC) is the UK’s leading social impact-led investor. Our mission is to grow the amount of money invested in tackling social issues and inequalities in the UK; we do this by investing ourselves and enabling others to invest for impact too. Since 2011, we have helped the social impact investment market grow twelve-fold to over £10 billion. This capital has financed social purpose organisations tackling everything from homelessness to mental health and fuel poverty. BSC manages £634m of its own investments as well as acting as portfolio manager for the Schroder BSC Social Impact Investment Trust (SBSI) managing its £83m portfolio. BSC also has a strategic goal of managing third party monies, as reflected in its role as delegated portfolio manager for the Schroders BSC Social Impact Trust PLC. As a key member of BSC’s Legal & Compliance team, this role would suit a lawyer with transactional experience, ideally with knowledge of funds, but who is also willing and able to support the wide variety of work covered by an in-house legal team. It will be a varied and exciting role with the ability to become involved and play an essential role in transactions at the forefront of social impact investing as well as supporting the growth and success of Better Society Capital as an organisation. The role will give the successful candidate broad exposure to all areas of BSC’s work supporting the Investment Group on investment activity but across the business on corporate, commercial, regulatory and governance matters alongside colleagues in the Legal & Compliance team. The role is offered full time on a fixed term contract for 12 months. Key Responsibilities: New Investments Participate in the due diligence process to ensure legal and regulatory issues around the structure of investments are understood and addressed. Support the Investment Group with term sheet discussions. Negotiation of legal documentation, working with different team members across BSC, co-investors and external counsel, and assist with the completion and onboarding process for investments. Existing Investments Maintain a knowledge of BSC’s legal and regulatory obligations relating to its investments and make sure BSC has all necessary legal investment documentation in place and properly recorded/stored. Participate in the management of investments over their lifetime, including any amendments or waivers. Advise on the process to restructure or exit investments. Ongoing support for the investment monitoring process with regard to any legal and regulatory issues that arise. Corporate, Governance and Regulatory Support colleagues across the office with legal, governance and regulatory queries. Support client investment initiatives, such as the firm’s role as portfolio manager for the listed investment trust, Schroders BSC Social Impact Trust plc. Review legislation and regulatory changes and support the implementation of consequential policies, procedures and training. Draft and negotiate commercial contracts (including NDAs). Work with colleagues in the Legal & Compliance team to build and share know-how and best practice across BSC and its portfolio companies, including training and templates. Manage the relationships, including costs, with external counsel. Generally, take a proactive and enthusiastic role in helping to develop the Legal & Compliance team, including continually looking to improve our working practices and embracing technological improvements (including adoption of AI), all with the goal of providing top quality support for all of BSC and thereby helping to deliver on BSC’s mandate. Other Participate in at least one ‘BSC Citizenship’ activity, helping to make BSC a great place to work. This could be helping to organise our summer or winter social, joining the Staff Council or helping with health and safety. Skills and Experience: Essential Qualifications & Experience Solicitor qualified in England and Wales. Legal related project management. Desirable Qualifications & Experience Knowledge and experience of transactional finance. Knowledge and experience of private and/or public market investment funds. Knowledge and experience of financial services regulation. Knowledge and experience of data protection. Engagement with the third sector in some capacity (e.g., trustee of a charity). Skills, Abilities and Attributes Confident, effective communicator who is approachable and flexible. Can deal effectively with senior management. Systematic approach to work with high attention to detail. Strong research and analytical skills. Enthusiastic proponent of technical development of legal operations (including AI). Approachable and strong team player but able to work self-sufficiently. Flexible and willing to take on different tasks as required. Enthusiastic and proactive with the confidence to influence at all levels. Resilient and can cope with ambiguity and change. Well organised and able to prioritise. Good at finding innovative solutions to problems. Ability to identify risk with sound commercial awareness. Commitment to continuous learning and development. Better Society Capital core values are: Purposeful – We are passionate and energetic in our work to bring about our long-term vision of a thriving social investment market that enables positive social impact. Pioneering Spirit – We give our team the autonomy and flexibility to be entrepreneurial and creative. We have the courage to push boundaries and a restless drive for change. Openness – We listen, learn, experiment and collaborate. And we are adaptive and flexible in responding to what we learn. Rigorous – We take a rigorous approach in all we do. We expect the highest standards and continually strive for excellence. Respectful – We are genuine in both our approach and aspiration. We value each member of our team and our partners for what they bring. Please send your CV and Cover Letter (up to one A4 page) to Careers4Change. Right to Work: Candidates need to have the existing right to work in the UK. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion: Better Society Capital is committed to being a diverse organisation that is truly representative of the communities we serve. We therefore welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds, particularly those under-represented in the social impact investment sector (e.g. people from LGBTQIA+, racialised, disabled, or under-served communities) Better Society Capital is an equal opportunities employer with an inclusive environment where all employees can contribute to their fullest potential. We want every colleague to be able to deliver their work with dignity, equality, comfort and independence. Our office is fully accessible with step-free access and an open-plan set up. We are open to accommodation requests regarding assistive technologies, accessibility tools, flexible working or any other reasonable adjustments that will make working or visiting here more accessible for you.

item.title: Office and Administration Assistant
item.description: Office & Administration Assistant – Key Responsibilities Office management and administration Maintain a welcoming, safe and efficient office environment that enables staff, volunteers and visitors to work effectively, in line with the ‘Groundswellian Way’, our coproduced principles for a safe, positive work culture. Manage the day-to-day running of the office, including , refreshments, office supplies, IT equipment, room bookings and reception duties. Build positive working relationships with Workspace, office contractors and suppliers, including cleaners, maintenance providers and other building services. Facilities, health and safety Ensure all staff and volunteers receive relevant health and safety information during induction, including access to the health & Safety training video, awareness of fire procedures, emergency evacuation routes and workplace safety responsibilities. Coordinate the maintenance and servicing of Groundswell's office equipment, facilities and assets, ensuring they remain safe, functional and fit for purpose. IT and Systems Organisational administration Provide administrative support for organisational meetings, events and activities, including venue bookings, catering, logistics and preparation of materials. Provide governance administration, including scheduling Board and Committee meetings, preparing meeting logistics, taking accurate minutes and maintaining action logs. Provide administrative support to the Chief Executive, Trustees and Senior Leadership Team, including diary coordination, meeting arrangements and room bookings. General Maintain accurate administrative systems, records and filing, ensuring information is organised, confidential and GDPR compliant. Build positive relationships across the organisation, providing responsive, friendly and professional support to colleagues, volunteers and external stakeholders. Groundswell responsibilities and the Groundswellian Way Act in line with our Code of Conduct and the Groundswellian Way in all interactions with colleagues, volunteers, partners and visitors. We want to: Person Specification Essential Desirable Why join Groundswell? Key Benefits Culture Application and Interview Process Please let us know if you would like to request any accommodations or adjustments throughout the application and interview process. We will be very happy to support these wherever possible to give all applicants the best opportunity to showcase their skills and experience. We encourage our candidates to draw from their personal and professional experiences, skills, knowledge and passion for our work in their applications, as we believe this will be the best representation of why you are the right fit for the role. While we acknowledge that Generative AI can be a useful tool when used selectively, we do not believe it can replace the authenticity that each individual can bring to their application. Therefore, we ask you to consider carefully any use of Generative AI throughout the application process. Application To apply please follow this link: Please submit your CV along with a cover letter stating: You can find a guide to writing your cover letter here , which includes some tips and general guidance. The deadline for applications is 10am on Monday 17 th August. Interviews Interviews will be held in person on either Wednesday 2 nd or Thursday 3 rd September. We are a small charity with limited resources and are unable to give individualised feedback on unsuccessful applications before the interview stage. Pre-employment checks The job offer for the successful candidate will be subject to a reference check. Many thanks for taking the time to look into this role – it is an exciting opportunity, and we hope you will consider applying.

item.title: Portfolio Manager (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Impact on Urban Health is part of Guy’s & St Thomas’ Foundation. Our collective mission is to build the foundations of a healthier society. As a member of the team, you have a real opportunity to shape our work and the impact we can have. This is fuelled by our desire to be more than the sum of our parts. We’re curious, we think big and we’re not afraid to take risks. As part of our team, you will work alongside talented people from a mix of personal and professional backgrounds. We are a Living Wage employer and support flexible working, part-time roles and job shares. Though our ambitions are serious, this is a friendly place to work with lots of opportunities to meet and socialise with colleagues. We believe there is immense power in diversity and aim to recruit and nurture talent who think and act differently. There is more information about working with us on our website where you can find out: How we approach recruitment Our team, culture and values The benefits of working with us Our approach to diversity, equity & inclusion, health & wellbeing, and learning & development The Innovation Manager supports the Director of Innovation to execute core parts of the innovation strategy by embedding improved delivery practices and test-and-learn capabilities across Impact on Urban Health and, where relevant, the wider Foundation, overseeing a priority set of cross-IoUH and within-programme innovation projects. At Impact on Urban Health, we are building a portfolio of programmes that demonstrate the power of long-term approaches to complex health issues in urban environments. We focus our efforts on the London boroughs of Lambeth and Southwark, working in partnership with residents, local and national government, and community and private sector partners to improve the health of local residents. By doing this, we aim to influence others in the UK and internationally to create better health. The programmes focus on children’s health and food, financial foundations for adult health, the health effects of air pollution, and children’s mental health; and are all at different stages of development. A Portfolio Manager builds part of a programme strategy, co-develops projects with partners, makes recommendations for funding these projects, and proactively manages the end-to-end partnership and funding lifecycle. This is a supported process, with lots of input and ideas shared across the team as the Portfolio Managers shape their projects. We build partnerships with a wide range of partners, from local communities, businesses, charities, the public sector and any other person or organisation that we think can have an impact on health equity. Key Responsibilities Strategy and Programme Development: Build a deep understanding of the health issues your programme focuses on and the relevant systems that need to change to achieve greater equity. Collaborate with our Data, Evaluation & Learning team to understand different forms of evidence and lived experience relevant to your programme. Lead on strategy development for part of one or more of our urban health programmes. Identify organisations with whom to collaborate. Partnership and Funding Lifecycle: Lead the funding partnership life cycle. This includes: Developing ideas and partnerships Approach relevant organisations and their teams, engaging them and co-developing projects and partnerships that support the delivery of our impact goals and programmatic strategies. Apply equitable funding principles in practice, including transparency, fairness, trust-building and power-sharing with partners. Bringing partnerships through our decision-making process and contracting. Drive an inclusive/non-extractive due diligence process. Detail clear specifications and deliverables for projects which align with the relevant urban health programme. Deliver presentations at Executive Investment Committee meeting. Draft funding (grant giving) contracts using templates. Managing and exiting partnerships Guide, advise and learn from existing project partners as they deliver to achieve our mutual goals. Utilise effective programme management techniques to monitor effective delivery against contracts and specifications. Ensure project partners report against agreed deliverables as required within contracts, and scrutinise to ensure that contracts are being fulfilled. Proactively address any areas where contracts are not being delivered upon, escalating where necessary. Work with our Data, Evaluation & Learning team and external evaluation experts to develop and deliver evaluation plans for projects and partnerships. Assist organisational development of partners, through commissioning grants plus support. Scaling Impact, Influence and Thought Leadership: Plan and deliver ways to scale solutions and grow impact through influencing, in collaboration with partners and internal teams across the organisation, such as Policy, Influencing & Communications, and Data, Evaluation & Learning. This includes: Building diverse, cross-sector partnerships Formulating plans to scale the impact of your portfolio Convening and supporting partners to work together to influence policy and decision-makers Delivering thought leadership for your area of focus to influence relevant stakeholders, e.g. blog writing, attending and speaking at events. Contribute to strategic communications, campaigning and influencing activity where relevant. Role responsibilities are not exhaustive, and you would be reasonably expected to take on wider tasks that are commensurate with the level of your role Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Skills, abilities and attributes: Demonstrable commitment to equity and good health for all, in particular those affected by poverty and racism Ability to draft robust contracts from templates. Inclusive and high-quality communication and influencing skills, including strong presentation skills. Strategic thinking and problem-solving skills – able to come up with solutions to complex problems. Strong relationship building skills and ability to engage a wide range of audiences including effective community engagement. Ability to manage uncertainty, navigate complexity, seek clarity and actively ensure roles and responsibilities are clear. Commercial acumen (though we will support you to develop this). Knowledge, experience, and qualifications: Experience / proven ability in programme / project management. Demonstrable understanding of philanthropy, grant giving processes and practice. An understanding or experience of a range of different entities and organisations, for example local, national, international organisations, voluntary or community organisations, social enterprises, government, policy makers, businesses, statutory bodies. An understanding of what makes funded / grass roots organisations effective in the work they lead. Experience in community organising, asset ownership or asset stewardship (desirable) An understanding of community wealth building principles in the context of place regeneration (desirable) Experience in blended finance capital stacks (desirable) Experience in or knowledge of one or more of the following areas will be desirable: Experience of working or living in diverse urban areas. The healthcare system and how it affects local communities. Public policy and regulations. Private sector advocacy and lobbying. Innovation Benefits Contributory pension Annual personal development budget Annual health and wellbeing personal allowance Enhanced maternity, paternity, and parental leave pay accessible without length of service requirements. Health and wellbeing programme that offers optional free yearly health check-ups. Support for healthy eating via fruit bowls and onsite lunch facilities. Agile working, flexible hours, and supportive IT kit. Shower facilities and bike lock area. Generous annual leave (27 days + bank holidays) Subsidies for glasses Employee Assistance Programme

item.title: Advice Manager
item.description: About Toynbee Hall Based in the East End of London since 1884, Toynbee Hall is a charity working alongside people facing poverty, injustice, and inequality to build a fairer East London. We provide vital advice and support, working in partnership to tackle unfairness and ensure everyone has an equal chance to thrive. Team Background The Debt Advice Team at Toynbee Hall provides crucial support to individuals and families struggling with financial burdens. Funded by the Money and Pensions Service (MaPS), this team delivers expert guidance and practical solutions to help clients manage and reduce their debt. Key Responsibilities Management of local sites to ensure all services are available. Ensure local services are available daily by effectively managing staffing, sickness, annual leave, emergencies and operational challenges. Work closely with internal teams, external contractors and local stakeholders to ensure all sites operate safely, efficiently and in line with organisational standards. Line management of a team to ensure objectives are set and met. Lead, motivate and support the team to achieve agreed service, quality, compliance and performance objectives. Conduct regular one-to-one supervision, team meetings and performance reviews, providing constructive feedback and clear expectations. Ensure compliance and the quality of advice required are achieved. Ensure the team consistently delivers high-quality, client-focused debt advice in line with FCA requirements, funder expectations and Toynbee Hall policies. Monitor case quality through audits, supervision, management information and performance data, implementing improvement plans where required. Contribute to the team Be an active member of the Advice Services management team, contributing to service planning, operational improvements and organisational change. Work collaboratively with funders, partner organisations and colleagues across Toynbee Hall to support strategic priorities, projects and service development. Other Provide visible leadership across multiple Toynbee Hall locations, ensuring consistency of culture, service delivery and operational standards. Travel across London as required, and occasionally elsewhere in the UK. Person Specification The successful candidate will demonstrate: Essential Criteria Experience and Skills Significant experience of managing frontline advice services and leading high-performing teams. Proven ability to provide technical supervision and support on complex debt advice cases. Up-to-date knowledge of debt advice legislation, FCA requirements, funding compliance and sector best practice. Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office and case management systems. Hold a recognised debt advice qualification (e.g. CertMAP or equivalent) with demonstrable experience of delivering and supervising FCA-regulated debt advice services. Communication and Interpersonal Skills Excellent leadership, communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate others. Ability to build positive relationships with colleagues, partners, funders and external stakeholders. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Personal Attributes Inclusive, collaborative and approachable leadership style. Highly organised, proactive and solutions focused. Calm and resilient under pressure, with the ability to make informed decisions. Commitment Demonstrates a strong commitment to Toynbee Hall’s mission, values and strategic objectives. Willingness to work across multiple Toynbee Hall and community locations. Willingness to undertake relevant training, including safeguarding and regulatory requirements. Please note the right to work in the UK is a requirement of this role. Please refer to the attached job description for more details.

item.title: Trading Support Assistant
item.description: Job Advert Who are we? NUS is a confederation of over 440 students’ unions representing just under 4m students and apprentices across Scotland, England, Northern Ireland and Wales. In Scotland, there are over 40 students’ associations representing 460,000 students. NUS Charity is an exciting organisation developing and championing strong students’ unions. We connect our members and curate services to deliver advice, guidance and crisis support to students’ unions. We do professional differently. We are a progressive charity representing students’ unions across the UK. The sector is inclusive, fun, dynamic and representative and we put students and students’ unions at the heart of everything we do. We are challenging but are committed to creating a supportive and flexible environment which pushes your personal development in your everyday activity. What we do Students’ unions can be transformational hubs for students, staff, and wider society. NUS Charity support our member’s development to enhance their capacity and harness opportunities to maximise their positive impact. We do this in many ways, from managing a purchasing consortium to drive great value for our members, to our development activity, supporting the best potential in students’ unions - we strive to make a difference to our members. The student movement is fast-paced and sometimes challenging, but we’re also a big family who support each other. We’re see anti-oppression as central to our mission. Education isn’t working unless it’s working for everyone in our society. We’re trans inclusive without exception. And we welcome individuals who are up for taking active responsibility for their own ongoing learning on liberation, equity, diversity and inclusion. What’s the job? The Trading Support Assistant role is a full time, permanent post within the Trading Support Department. Your purpose will be to provide administrative support to the central billing team, working across several different teams, and getting relevant information from suppliers where required. In this role, you will provide administrative support to the trading support team and review product lines, inputting and checking information across multiple systems. This will involve taking in information from different sources and entering it into a variety of different systems, making attention to detail and logic crucial skills for success. You will also act as one of the points of contact within NUS’s relationship with students’ unions who are part of the purchasing consortium and with administrative service providers, such as Focus IT. Furthermore, you will act as one of the points of contact within NUS’s relationship with suppliers to ensure that relevant sustainability information is provided through the tender processes. You will report to the Central Billing Manager. Other responsibilities include maintaining awareness of and acting within agreed processes and procedures for central billing and contract administration, undertaking all necessary duties and activities to deliver the role’s responsibilities, alerting the Central Billing Manager to any barriers encountered and contributing to the successful resolution of any issues. You will also be expected to actively engage in individual and team professional development activities, carry out responsibilities in a resource-efficient manner, and adhere to NUS policies and practices, actively supporting and promoting the NUS vision, mission and objectives. Who you are To succeed in this role, you’ll need to demonstrate a comprehensive blend of experience, knowledge, skills, and attributes. Essential qualifications and experience for this position include A level equivalent experience and Microsoft Office Word and Excel experience. You must possess good IT knowledge, including Outlook, good data entry skills, and the ability to demonstrate good communication skills. The ability to work with little supervision is essential, as is being organised, logical, and analytical in all aspects of work. Finally, regarding attributes, you must demonstrate a commitment to being an active part of an environment that promotes equality of opportunity whilst recognising and valuing diversity, and the ability to keep focused and maintain a high level of attention to detail. This is a full time, permanent post. Your normal place of work will be Stockport, and we support hybrid working and flexible working requests. Why apply? As well as a great place to work, we offer a range of benefits including: Generous holiday entitlement (starting at 27 days per year rising with service to 30 days, pro rata for part time) Enhanced sick, maternity, paternity, shared parental and adoption pay Paid volunteer days Health Cash Plan Pension scheme with employer matched contributions up to 6% Employee Assistance Scheme Cycle to Work Scheme Childcare Allowance Paid volunteering days- three days per year for full time staff We aim to practice what we preach and offer a flexible person-centered working environment. We are open to considering requests for job-share or part-time working/ We are open to exploring flexible working patterns. We’re committed to equality of opportunity for all and we are explicitly trans inclusive. We welcome applications from individuals regardless of their race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, age, gender, or disability. You can be yourself here whoever you are, be proud of the work you do and build a career in a place that knows different is good. Please apply via our online application form, we are unable to accept CVs. If you are unable to complete or application due to accessibility needs please contact [email protected] . Closing date for applications is 21st August 2026 If you’re successfully shortlisted we’ll see you at an interview on 1st September 2026 Department Trading Support Contract type Permanent Hours 35 Salary £25,091 Benefits As well as a generous annual leave entitlement, we also have a range of policies focused on promoting work life balance. We offer other benefits including pension, EAP scheme and discounts. ref-229962

item.description: Job description We are looking for a communications officer on a 12 month fixed term contract to cover an internal secondment within our team. You will be an enthusiastic, creative individual who wants to pursue a career in communications. You will be excited by the prospect of improving and maximising our communications impact. You may be in the earlier stages of developing your career in communications and will be keen to learn, develop and hone a wide range of skills in digital communications, media, events management and publication production. Interest in and understanding of environmental policy and politics would be an asset. You will need excellent interpersonal skills as you will regularly liaise with our staff and support them in communicating their work. As an unflappable multi-tasker, you will be someone who enjoys managing varied work and who takes great pride in producing content to the highest standard and takes pleasure in achieving success as part of a team. Attention to detail and sound judgement are vital in this role to maintain Green Alliance’s brand integrity. item.title: Individual Giving Manager
item.description: Shape the future of Individual Giving at Heart Research UK and build lasting relationships that change lives. Job title : Individual Giving Manager Reporting to : Director of Income Generation Salary : £42,000 per annum Hours : Permanent, 37 hours per week, flexible working requests will be considered Location : Hybrid within commutable distance to our Head Office in Leeds Interviews to take place in our central Leeds Office on Thursday 27 August 2026. About Heart Research UK We are Heart Research UK. Every 5 minutes, someone dies from heart diseases in the UK. It’s likely that heart diseases will impact all of our lives one day, if they haven’t already done so. We need to tackle this problem head on, and we need to start today. Donations from the public fund lifesaving medical research to find new treatments and cures, and support people across the UK to keep their hearts healthy. But people are still dying. Together, we will prevent, treat and cure heart diseases through research, education and community support. Until there are no more deaths from heart diseases. Job Description The Individual Giving Manager will build a programme with enormous growth potential. Working closely with the Director of Fundraising and colleagues across the charity, you will develop the Individual Giving strategy for Heart Research UK, establishing a robust programme of donor acquisition and supporter development, while focusing equally on supporter experience and retention to inspire long-term giving. The Individual Giving Manager will be comfortable balancing strategic thinking and planning with hands-on delivery. They will have experience in using audience insight, data and continuous testing to identify the channels and products that deliver the greatest long-term value. They will focus on establishing a test, learn, tweak, test again culture that is driven by evidence, insight and return on investment. Given the nature of the role, it will require the postholder to be able to manage their time and workload effectively across a variety of tasks, while actively contributing to our work to generate income and achieve our targets. Key Responsibilities · Work with the Director of Income Generation to develop and deliver an ambitious Individual Giving strategy that supports Heart Research UK’s fundraising and organisational growth objectives · Develop and deliver acquisition activities already identified for the coming year, and identify opportunities for developing new products and propositions in the medium to long-term, focussing on meeting supporter needs and delivering sustainable income · Develop an acquisition programme using a mix of digital and offline channels including: o Paid social, search and other google platforms, email o Direct mail – both warm and cold o DRTV o Lottery o Face to face o Telemarketing · Utilise modelling tools to secure investment for test, learn and optimisation activities, and then to forecast and reforecast returns on those activities as they progress. Using this insight, recommend future investment. · Work with the CRM Manager to develop supporter journeys that maximise engagement, retention and lifetime value, and deliver the highest standards of supporter experience across channels · Identify opportunities to deepen supporter relationships through cross-sell, upgrade and reactivation activity · Lead relationships with third party agencies, following procurement procedures and managing agencies to ensure Heart Research UK gets the most value for our investment and that agencies behave in line with our values and policies · Work with the Director of Income Generation to create and monitor budgets and forecasts, monitoring financial performance and contributing to annual budget cycles as well as longer-term forecasting · Work collaboratively with colleagues across fundraising, communications and data to deliver activities, utilising project management tools and the CRM to ensure clear expectation setting and time management and to avoid project creep · Share knowledge and champion best practice in Individual Giving and supporter insight across the organisation, for example identifying opportunities from within the Individual Giving programme to promote legacy giving, and contributing to the ongoing strategic development of the fundraising team · Ensure all fundraising activity complies with relevant legislation such as GDPR, and adheres to the Fundraising Code of Practice as well as Heart Research UK’s fundraising policies Our values Our values reflect who we are as a charity. We are dedicated to fundraising ethically, and to ensuring that the money our supporters donate is spent in the best way possible. Trustworthy – We do what we say we will and explain why if we can’t. When people choose to give us their money, we ensure we spend it wisely on projects that are most important to those affected by heart diseases. We are clear about what we expect from our people, and we support them in work and life. Ambitious – We want to bring an end to all heart diseases and on our journey, we want to help as many people as possible to live healthier and longer lives. We want to raise more so we can do more. We know that as a smaller organisation some people will stay with us for the ride while others will move on – we support the development of our teams so they can achieve their goals. We encourage new ways of doing things and know that we won’t always get it right, but we will learn from everything we do. Passionate – We believe in what we are doing, no one should die from heart diseases. We are doing everything we can to help save lives. We embrace emotion! We want to support everyone – to have innovative ideas that bring change and promote growth. Our people can be confident that we have their back, and they can enjoy their time with us. Our people: We are currently a team of 44 people and growing. Since the pandemic, we have moved to a hybrid working model, with some of our team members working remotely, with occasional trips to our Leeds office, and travel to events around the UK. We look after our team and have developed a number of wellbeing initiatives to help support our staff. This includes regular wellbeing sessions which cover various themes such as sleeping well, nutrition and goal setting, as well as a range of other staff benefits. This is an exciting time to join the charity as we are now in the second year of our five-year strategy, building on our ambitions to make an even bigger difference to the lives of people developing or dying from heart diseases. We are clear that to achieve our mission, we need to invest in long-term, sustainable income growth. We are looking for an ambitious and experienced Individual Giving Manager to lead the development of our Individual Giving programme; someone to join our energetic, collaborative, and dedicated team. Someone who will contribute to our culture and have the drive and passion to help us achieve our ambitious goals.
item.dc:creator: Heart Research UK

item.title: Director of Finance and Resources
item.description: Help shape the future of international development. Location: Hybrid (minimum one day per month in our London office – with the occasional need to attend additional in-person meetings) Reports to: Chief Executive Help shape the future of international development. Location: Hybrid (minimum one day per month in our London office – with the occasional need to attend additional in-person meetings) Reports to: Chief Executive Finance isn't just about numbers. It's about making change possible. At Bond, we believe a more just and equitable world is possible. As the UK network for organisations working in international development, we bring together more than 300 civil society organisations united by a shared ambition: to tackle poverty, inequality and injustice around the world. We champion the sector, influence policy, strengthen organisations and create the connections that enable our members to achieve greater impact together. International development is changing. Funding is becoming more complex. Expectations are growing. Organisations are navigating increasing uncertainty while responding to global crises that demand collaboration, innovation and resilience. That is why we're looking for an exceptional Director of Finance & Resources. This is a rare opportunity to join our Senior Management Team and help shape the future of Bond at a pivotal moment in our journey. A leadership role with purpose As our Director of Finance & Resources, you'll do far more than lead finance. You'll help ensure Bond remains financially resilient, operationally strong and strategically focused so that we can continue supporting the organisations working to create lasting global change. Working closely with our CEO, Trustees and senior colleagues, you'll provide the financial leadership, organisational insight and strategic challenge that enables confident decision-making across the organisation. You'll oversee Finance, Planning, Operations, HR and IT, ensuring the systems, people and financial governance behind our work are as strong as the mission we exist to serve. What you'll be doing You'll lead: Our long-term financial strategy and organisational planning. Annual budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting. Financial sustainability across both restricted and unrestricted funding. Board reporting and support to our Finance, Audit & Risk Committee. Risk management, company secretarial and organisational compliance. Finance, Operations and HR leadership. Grant budgeting, reporting and organisational cost recovery. Strategic planning that enables teams to maximise their impact. This is a role for someone equally comfortable presenting to Trustees, supporting colleagues with complex funding proposals, reviewing organisational risk, or rolling up their sleeves to solve operational challenges. Who we're looking for You're an experienced finance leader who understands that great organisations need both strong financial stewardship and ambitious thinking. You'll be a qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) with senior leadership experience and an ability to balance strategic oversight with practical delivery. You'll bring: Significant experience leading finance within a complex organisation. Strong understanding of charity finance and grant management. Experience working with Boards and Trustees. Outstanding planning, analytical and leadership skills. Experience leading multidisciplinary teams. A collaborative approach and the ability to build trusted relationships across an organisation. Most importantly, you'll share our commitment to equity, inclusion and creating positive change. We're looking for someone who sees finance not as a control function, but as a catalyst for organisational impact. Why Bond? Everything we do is rooted in collaboration. You'll join an organisation that believes lasting change happens when people come together, share expertise and challenge one another to do better. Alongside meaningful work, we offer: Hybrid working with flexibility built around trust. 27 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, a day off for your birthday and additional Christmas closure. 7% employer pension contribution. Learning and development opportunities. Comprehensive health and wellbeing support. A welcoming, inclusive and values-driven culture where everyone can thrive. Join us This is more than a finance leadership role. It's an opportunity to help strengthen the organisations working to build a fairer, more sustainable world. If you're looking for a role where your financial expertise can support meaningful change on a national and global scale, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV and a supporting statement explaining why you'd like to join Bond and what you'll bring to the role. We are partnering exclusively with Bryony Thomas at Allen Lane. For an informal conversation about the role, get in touch via the agency website.

item.title: Screening Co-ordinator
item.description: CRY has an exciting new job opportunity! We are an established UK charity, which for 25+ years has proactively worked to prevent young sudden cardiac deaths through awareness, screening and research as well as supporting families following a young sudden cardiac death. We are looking to recruit 2x Screening Co-ordinators to join our wonderful Screening Department. You will have: o A good, clear telephone voice with excellent spoken and written English o Good administration skills with an eye for detail. o The ability to interact well with a variety of stakeholders and CRY staff at all levels, and with many-and-varied external contacts and clients. o Excellent organisational skills with the ability to be flexible in managing tasks and workload on a daily basis. o The ability to remain calm and interact sensitively with any enquirers who may be anxious, stressed, upset, etc. o An appreciation for the need to treat personal data and medical information with the greatest of care in order to meet data protection and information security requirements. Main Duties: Coordinating your allocated CRY cardiac screening events which includes: o Being the main point of contact for the family, school or other party that is funding or requesting the screening event. o Liaising with the CRY Screening Managers / Drivers / Bookings Coordinator with all details regarding the event. o Working with and managing the online booking system for your CRY screening events. o Confirming event information and updating the screening spreadsheet (known as the ‘Screening Calendar’) with any changes. o Producing screening posters via Canva to advertise screening events. o Producing results letters, mail-merging letters and ensuring they are created and sent in a timely manner. o Managing email distribution lists (waiting lists) for individuals who wish to be notified about future screening events in their area; including updating the lists as needed and sending notifications when new event dates are released. o Ensuring all equipment and consumables are ready for the screening event and all prepared for the Driver to take on the CRY van. o Managing and inputting data into various CRY screening spreadsheets – e.g. producing information spreadsheets for use by the screening team on the day of the screening event. Ad hoc Duties: o Providing support to other members of the screening team with their assigned CRY screening events when needed (e.g. to cover annual leave, sickness, etc). o Answering telephone queries and emails about screening. o Secondary telephone answering duties for both the screening phone number and the main CRY office phone number. o Secondary ‘ECG’ mailbox answering duties. o Ensuring that records (physical and digital) are kept in accordance with general data protection and information security regulations (GDPR and related legislation) o Other office administration tasks at the request of the Screening Team Leader, Screening Manager or the Director of Screening and Research. Essential skills: o Confidence using Microsoft Office - particularly Outlook, Word and Excel. o Reliability o Attention to detail o Excellent telephone manner o Flexibility o Good organizational skills o Good interpersonal skills o Team working and a helpful attitude / demeanour o Confidentiality o Appreciation of the sensitive nature of CRY’s work Benefits: o Private Healthcare o 28 days of annual leave, inc. Bank Holidays. . o Long service bonus scheme (+ an additional half day per year of service, capped at 10 extra days). o Enhanced sick leave o Flexible lieu time system o Free car parking at the CRY office. o Workplace Pension scheme (3% CRY contributions). It is CRY policy to maintain a quality management system designed to meet the requirements of ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 in pursuit of its primary objectives. CRY’s Quality and Information Security Management Systems Manual defines our quality objectives and key procedures. The requirements of CRY’s quality and information security management system are mandatory; and all employees have a responsibility and obligation to read and adhere to all documentation they are provided with which relates to it. This will include, but is not limited to: IT security information; process documents for tasks; safety information; incident reporting processes; data protection requirements. Employees should demonstrate a practical application of the key objectives, where appropriate, in their daily duties. Advert closes: Monday 3rd Aug @ 00:00 Sifting: from w/c 3rd Aug Interviews: from 17th Aug
item.dc:creator: Cardiac Risk in the Young, Leatherhead

item.title: Partnerships Manager
item.description: Help shape the future of Ocean Literacy. We're looking for a commercially minded Partnerships Manager to grow our portfolio of corporate supporters and trusts while developing new partnerships that generate sustainable income. If you're an experienced relationship-builder who thrives on creating meaningful partnerships and generating income for a cause you care about, we'd love to hear from you. About Ocean Generation Ocean Generation is a UNESCO-endorsed Ocean education charity turning Science into Storytelling. We make Ocean Literacy accessible through film, pop-culture, and education programmes that empower practical action. Most people grow up unaware that the Ocean is keeping us all alive: Ocean Generation exists to change that. Established in 2009 by film producer Jo Ruxton MBE, our award-winning documentary ‘A Plastic Ocean’, was named by Sir David Attenborough as “one of the most important films of our time” and ignited mass public awareness about the impact of plastic pollution. Today, we address a full range of human-made threats impacting the Ocean, with a particular focus on programmes for young people across the world. Our Ocean Intelligence approach, how we translate complex Ocean science into engaging content through Science and Storytelling, has been endorsed by the Intergovernmental Oceanic Commission of UNESCO as a project under the UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development. Our vision is a world where society understands, values and acts for the Ocean. Our mission is to improve Ocean Literacy by translating complex science into engaging content, programmes and practical actions. As our Partnerships Manager, you'll help secure the funding that enables more people around the world to understand, value and act for the Ocean. Role Summary This is an exciting opportunity to join a small, ambitious charity where you'll have genuine ownership of a portfolio of corporate partners and trust funders while helping to shape Ocean Generation's fundraising strategy and long-term growth. Account Management & Stewardship Manage and grow a portfolio of corporate partners and selected trusts and foundations, delivering excellent relationship management, stewardship and reporting. Prepare and deliver high-quality partnership reports, impact updates and funding reports that demonstrate the value of support and strengthen long-term relationships. Act as the Funding Relationship Lead for their portfolio, ensuring reporting commitments, stewardship activity and internal coordination are managed throughout the life of each partnership or grant. Identify opportunities to renew, grow and enhance existing partnerships, maximising income and engagement. Maintain accurate partnership activity, reporting deadlines and pipeline information within Salesforce, monitor partnership performance, manage the fundraising pipeline, and contribute to income forecasting and pipeline reporting. In addition to partnership management responsibilities, manage community fundraising activities and events when required, contributing to the wider fundraising programme. Business Development & Income Generation Develop and secure new corporate partnerships by identifying, cultivating and converting prospective supporters into long-term partners. Prepare compelling funding proposals, partnership pitches and applications tailored to corporate and trust funding opportunities. Develop attractive ESG partnership opportunities and other funding propositions that align with Ocean Generation's mission and strategic priorities. Work closely with the Co-Executive Director (Partnerships) and Philanthropy Lead to identify, develop and secure strategic fundraising opportunities. Partnership Activation & Organisational Collaboration Collaborate with colleagues across the organisation to develop engaging partnership opportunities and ensure the successful delivery of partner benefits. Work with the Communications team to create partnership resources, campaigns, newsletters and impact content/case studies that strengthen engagement and increase visibility. Ensure fundraising activity complies with charity regulations, fundraising best practice, and Ocean Generation's values and ethical standards. Contribute as a proactive member of a small, agile team, supporting colleagues and identifying opportunities to maximise the impact and profile of fundraising activity. Skills & Experience Required Essential Experience in corporate fundraising, partnerships, business development/sales or account management. Proven ability to secure, manage and grow fundraising partnerships to achieve income targets. Excellent relationship management, communication and proposal writing skills. Strong organisational skills, with experience using a CRM and managing multiple priorities. Commercially minded, proactive and able to work independently within a small team. Confident interpreting budgets and fundraising performance data. Desirable Some experience working with trusts and foundations and/or major donors. Knowledge of ESG, CSR or corporate fundraising partnerships. Experience using a fundraising CRM such as Salesforce, Beacon or Raiser's Edge. An interest in environmental or conservation issues and a commitment to Ocean Generation's mission. Educated to degree level or equivalent professional experience. What We Offer Salary of £30,000–£35,000 per annum, depending on experience. A permanent role, full-time (37.5 hours per week), with consideration given to candidates seeking a part-time equivalent over four days. A flexible, remote-first working environment, with the freedom to work from anywhere in the UK. Core collaboration hours of 10am–4pm, Monday to Thursday, with flexibility over when you work your remaining hours. 25 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays (pro rata for part-time employees). A workplace pension scheme with automatic enrolment for eligible employees. A collaborative, ambitious and purpose-driven team committed to improving Ocean Literacy through science, storytelling and education. Opportunities for occasional UK travel to meet colleagues, partners and supporters. Application Deadline The closing date for applications is 5pm on Thursday 6 August 2026. We will review applications as they are received and reserve the right to close this vacancy early if sufficient applications are received. Early applications are therefore encouraged. Our Commitment to Inclusion Ocean Generation is committed to being an inclusive and equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. If there is anything we can do to make the application or interview process more accessible, please let us know.
item.dc:creator: Ocean Generation

item.title: Senior Fundraising Campaign Manager
item.description: Location: Flexible with home working option. Travel to London required. Contract type: Contracted (August 2026 – April 2027) Salary: £44,323.14 per annum Hours: 35 hours per week Closing Date: Thursday 6th August 2026 at 11:30pm Do you have experience leading complex, cross-organisational fundraising campaigns and the ability to bring multiple teams together around a shared goal? Are you a confident fundraiser and dynamic project manager who can balance strategic planning with hands-on delivery? Then join Shelter as Senior Fundraising Campaign Manager and lead the delivery of our flagship integrated fundraising campaign, the Winter Appeal. About the role As Senior Fundraising Campaign Manager, you will lead the planning and delivery of Shelter’s 2026 Winter Appeal — our largest integrated fundraising campaign and a vital contributor to the organisation’s financial sustainability. Working across Income Generation and with teams throughout Shelter and Shelter Scotland, you will bring together fundraising, media, marketing, digital, creative, campaigns, services and retail activity to maximise income, supporter acquisition and longer-term value. Alongside delivering the 2026 appeal against ambitious targets, you will work with the Head of Planning and Project Management to develop a multi-year Winter Appeal strategy. You will ensure future campaigns are supported by strong governance, clear milestones and robust plans that align with Shelter’s Income Generation strategy. This is a contracted role from August 2026 to April 2027. The role offers flexible and home-working options, with travel to London required. Role specifics We’re looking for an experienced campaign leader who can confidently matrix manage a complex, cross-organisational project team and keep delivery progressing against agreed timelines, budgets and objectives. You will oversee campaign governance, coordinate activity across multiple workstreams and ensure that marketing plans, media activity and creative content are fully aligned with the campaign’s audiences and objectives. You will identify opportunities, anticipate challenges and ensure risks or barriers are understood, escalated and resolved at the earliest opportunity. You will also own key project documentation, including campaign plans, governance arrangements, risk registers and stakeholder reports. As part of the role, you will line manage a Senior Project Management Executive, supporting their work across content development, creative delivery and performance reporting. Following the campaign, you will lead a full evaluation and establish clear, timebound improvement actions to strengthen future Winter Appeals. You may also support other organisational campaigns, acting as a fundraising representative and ensuring income generation is embedded within their development and delivery. Apply to be part of our team and help bring colleagues and supporters together in the fight for home. About you You will have experience project managing complex, cross-organisational income-generating projects and understand the opportunities and challenges involved in bringing multiple teams and priorities together. You will also have experience developing and delivering multi-year fundraising strategies, balancing long-term strategic thinking with the detailed, hands-on delivery needed to achieve results. You will be: A highly effective communicator with strong emotional intelligence Collaborative, flexible and diplomatic, while able to be assertive when required Confident influencing and negotiating with a wide range of stakeholders Comfortable moving between the fine detail and the bigger strategic picture Experienced in using a range of project management approaches, methodologies and tools Organised, proactive and able to bring energy and momentum to complex work Experience of leading multi-million-pound campaigns and working across fundraising, marketing, media or other integrated campaign disciplines would be particularly valuable. Benefits We offer a wide range of benefits, including 30 days of annual leave, enhanced family-friendly policies, a competitive pension scheme and interest-free travel loans. Our employees also have access to flexible working practices, salary sacrifice schemes, a tenancy deposit loan, payroll giving, a cycle-to-work scheme and an employee assistance programme. We are happy to talk about flexible working and personal growth, and we are committed to creating a workplace where you can be yourself and achieve success based on your merit. About the team This role sits within Fundraising Enablement in Shelter’s Income Generation Directorate and reports to the Head of Planning and Project Management. Fundraising Enablement provides direction, structure and specialist support to colleagues across the organisation, helping to deliver Shelter’s Income Generation strategic plan. Through expertise in planning, project management, innovation and fundraising compliance, the function enables teams to achieve their income-generating goals and supports an organisation-wide culture in which fundraising can thrive. You will work closely with colleagues across Individual Giving, High Value Partnerships, Community and Events, Retail, and Product Development and Innovation, as well as teams including Media, Creative, Digital, Campaigns, Services and Shelter Scotland. How to apply Please click ‘Apply for Job’ below. You are required to submit your work history and a supporting statement. The supporting statement should include your responses to the points in the ‘About You’ section of the job description of no more than 350 words each. Please provide specific examples following the STAR format and ensure you demonstrate how you address the behaviours below in your responses: We work together to achieve our shared purpose We create change and align behind our strategy We are open to risk and learning from our experiences About Shelter Home is a human right. It’s our foundation and where we thrive. Yet every day, millions of people are being devastated by the housing emergency. We exist to defend the right to a safe home. Because home is everything. We need ambitious, passionate people to join us. This is your chance to play a part in the fundamental change we are striving to achieve. Our enemy is the social injustice at the core of the escalating housing emergency. To win this fight, we must be representative of the people we are here to help and those who support our movement. In all our people decisions, we take pride in being inclusive, equitable and transparent. We are committed to combating racism both within and outside Shelter, and we welcome you on our journey to becoming a truly anti-racist organisation. We recognise that people from marginalised groups may face additional barriers throughout their careers. Research has shown that women and people of colour are less likely to apply for roles unless they feel they meet every requirement. If you are excited about this role but your experience does not align perfectly with every part of the job description, please do not let that stop you from applying. We encourage you to tell us how your skills, knowledge, behaviours and experience would support your success in the role. Safeguarding statement Safeguarding is everyone’s business. Shelter is committed to protecting the health, wellbeing and human rights of those we support and enabling them to live free from harm, abuse and neglect. All staff are expected to observe professional standards of behaviour and conduct their work in line with our Safeguarding Policies. Shelter does not accept unsolicited CVs from external recruitment agencies or accept the fees associated with them.
item.dc:creator: Shelter

item.title: Operations Officer - Wildlife (South)
item.description: The Woodland Trust is looking for an Operations Officer - Wildlife. This role will work collaboratively with colleagues across a number of teams, particularly in Operations and Nature Recovery, to advise and help deliver our plans to reduce adverse herbivore impacts (with an initial focus on deer populations) and make meaningful and lasting improvements to the woodland ecological condition of our estate. This role is based within the South and covers Central and Southern England along with Wales. A company vehicle will be provided for this role. This role requires a 4x4, which is a benefit in kind that is taxed at £300pcm. Alternatively, there is the option to opt out of having a company vehicle should you have a suitable vehicle of your own. Please note that our Company Vehicle Policy is also under review as part of our Job Families and Contract Review project, so the eligibility criteria therein are subject to change in due course. The Role: Provide expert advice, guidance and training to operational teams, ensuring delivery of evidence-led wildlife management interventions. Oversee safe, ethical and legally compliant wildlife management across the estate, always protecting organisational reputation. Support regional and national operations with wildlife management activities, communications and stakeholder engagement, maintaining sensitivity to public opinion. Work collaboratively with estate, outreach and conservation teams to deliver wildlife management programmes at scale in line with best practice and Health & Safety standards. Contribute specialist expertise to policy, advocacy and fundraising activities, supporting funding applications and influencing work through data and case studies. Deliver and evaluate wildlife and ecological surveys, ensuring accurate reporting and use of data to inform future operational decisions. Manage contracts, equipment (including firearms and drones) and compliance processes, ensuring adherence to legal and organisational standards. Build partnerships and identify opportunities for landscape-scale wildlife management, while maintaining professional development and awareness of best practice. This is a homebased role, requiring regular travel to locations within the Southern landscape, sometimes to remote locations. You would be expected to live within reasonable travelling distance of your area of responsibility. Occasional travel across the UK and overnight stays will be required. The Candidate: You’ll deliver hands-on wildlife management across estates, including the safe and compliant use of firearms in public-facing environments. You’ll plan, prioritise and coordinate operational wildlife work, ensuring teams deliver high standards efficiently under pressure. You’ll develop and deliver practical training programmes using varied learning methods, ensuring knowledge is embedded and monitored. Communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, including landowners, partners and community groups. Represent the organisation professionally both internally and externally, supporting operational teams and managing differing public perspectives. Work across large and remote areas, collaborating with teams or working independently to achieve conservation goals. Maintain accurate records and produce high-quality, evidence-based reports using Microsoft Office, databases and surveys. Manage external contracts and ensure compliance with health & safety standards, including risk assessments, documentation and safe equipment use. Benefits and Wellbeing: Joining our team means you’ll be a big part of tackling environmental and climate issues. We take good care of our staff, offering support and training opportunities. We also offer: Enhanced Employer Pension Life Assurance Flexible & Hybrid Working Options Generous Annual Leave - 25 Days Plus Bank Holidays (pro rata’d for part-time) Buy and Sell Holiday Scheme Enhanced Parental Pay Employee Assistance Programme About Us: The Woodland Trust is the UK’s largest woodland conservation charity. We want to see a world where trees and woods thrive for people and nature. The Trust engages and inspires people to make their difference tackling the nature and climate crisis helping protect, restore and create our vital woods and trees. Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: To achieve our vision of a world where woods and trees thrive for people and nature, we need to better reflect society and the communities we work in. All people, no matter their background, identity, ability, or circumstance, should benefit from trees. People of colour and disabled people are currently under-represented across the environment and conservation sector. If you identify as a person of colour and/or disabled, we particularly encourage you to apply. Please contact us to discuss any additional support or adjustments you may need to complete your application. Application Advice: For fairness we keep our candidates’ personal details hidden from the hiring managers, and we do not ask for your CV at application. Make sure that your Personal Statement clearly shows how your skills and knowledge link to the specifications in the job description and you share with us your passion for the role. Acceptable Use - Artificial Intelligence (AI): We understand that candidates may choose to use AI tools to support their job applications-for example, to help structure or edit written responses. We welcome the use of AI in this way, particularly where it helps improve accessibility, such as for neurodivergent applicants. However, we ask that any information submitted reflects your own experience, skills and understanding. During interviews, candidates are expected to respond independently without the use of AI tools. Apply Now: If you're ready to make a difference and grow with us, send in your application today. We might close the job opening early if we get a lot of applications, so it's a good idea to apply soon. If we do close the advert early, and you have an application in process, we will email you prior to closing to give you time to complete. Interviews will be held via Microsoft Teams on 24th & 25th August.
item.dc:creator: The Woodland Trust

item.title: Communications Manager
item.description: Communications Manager Young people's charity Temporary, 3 months £18.07 to £19.43 per hour, plus holiday pay 35 hours per week, 28 hours considered Hybrid, 2 days in London office Starting asap, interviews w/c 27 th online This is a fantastic opportunity to join a respected youth charity as Communications Manager, leading the delivery of digital communications across the organisation. Reporting to the Head of Communications and Policy and sitting within the Fundraising and Communications Directorate, you will play a key role in raising the charity's profile, engaging stakeholders, and ensuring impactful stories reach the right audiences. Charity People are looking for a hands-on communications professional who enjoys combining strategic thinking with practical delivery. You will lead the planning and management of digital communications, take ownership of the social media calendar, and ensure content is aligned with organisational priorities, campaigns, and key activities throughout the year. Working closely with colleagues across the charity, you will uncover and develop compelling stories that showcase the impact of programmes and initiatives, helping to build engagement across a range of audiences. The role will involve creating and commissioning high-quality content for social media, websites, email campaigns, newsletters, blogs, case studies, photography, and video projects. You will support communications activity linked to campaigns, events, policy, and public affairs work, while ensuring all channels remain active, engaging, and audience focused. Using insight, analytics, and performance data, you will continually evaluate and improve communications activity, helping to maximise reach and impact. The successful candidate will have experience managing website content and structure through a CMS, ideally WordPress, alongside strong knowledge of email marketing platforms such as Mailchimp. You will be confident planning, scheduling, and managing social media channels, particularly LinkedIn and Instagram, with a clear understanding of how to grow engagement and develop content that resonates with different audiences. Exceptional writing and storytelling skills are essential, together with the ability to adapt content for multiple channels and purposes. This role requires a proactive and organised communicator who can quickly get up to speed, take ownership of projects, and provide reliable support to the Head of Communications. You will be comfortable leading on campaigns, coordinating content plans with delivery teams, managing competing priorities, and ensuring communications activity continues to move forward at pace across the organisation. If you are a creative and driven communications professional looking to make a genuine difference through your work, this is an opportunity to join a passionate team dedicated to improving the lives of young people. Please apply without delay. This role closes on Monday 27 th July. Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

item.title: Health Advisor - Roving
item.description: Hours: You will be required to work the hours as are necessary for the proper discharge of the duties with the notional requirement being 35 hours per working week. Work will normally be undertaken in office hours, Monday to Friday, but weekend and evening working will be required Remuneration: Up to £42,440 GBP gross per annual (dependent on experience) Duration: 12 months, with the possibility of extension subject to funding Location: Manchester, UK (hybrid working available), with an expectation of up to 80% international travel/deployment as required by UK-Med. (Open to candidates based in the UK or internationally, with a preference for UK-based candidates due to operational considerations.) We are seeking a Medical Doctor with expertise and experience in international humanitarian responses, conflict and/or disasters to provide expert technical leadership across UK-Med’s growing portfolio of emergency health programmes. UK-Med is a frontline humanitarian medical NGO, delivering life-saving healthcare in emergencies and strengthening health systems in some of the world’s most challenging environments. As a key partner of the UK Emergency Medical Team (UK EMT), we work closely with the UK Government, WHO, Ministries of Health and international partners to respond rapidly when crises strike. This is a unique opportunity for a highly experienced humanitarian clinician who is passionate about emergency response and willing to deploy internationally in support of UK-Med’s operations. Our teams have responded to some of the world's most complex humanitarian crises, including conflicts, disease outbreaks, natural disasters and public health emergencies. Current and recent programmes have included conflict responses in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan, as well as support to Ebola preparedness and response activities in DRC, and disaster responses in countries including Venezuela. The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping humanitarian health programmes, providing technical expertise, supporting programme design and strategy, contributing to funding proposals and deploying overseas to provide leadership to multidisciplinary health teams when required. You will bring significant experience in emergency and humanitarian health, strong technical credibility and the ability to work effectively with health authorities, WHO and international partners in complex and fast-moving environments. Join us and be part of a passionate, purpose-driven organisation making a real difference where healthcare is needed most. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, a supportive and collaborative working environment, and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to humanitarian health outcomes worldwide. UK-Med is a dynamic and ambitious organisation with a dedicated team of staff, volunteers and Register members committed to delivering high-quality healthcare where it is needed most. How to apply We strongly recommend that you read the Candidate Information Pack - Health Advisor - roving - July 2026 before applying for this role. To apply, please submit a current CV and a supporting letter (no more than 2 pages) that includes a detailed explanation of your suitability for this post with specific reference to the essential criteria in the person specification. Applications must be submitted through our online jobs portal no later than Monday 10th of August 2026 Please note that this is a rolling recruitment process. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis and hiring manager will review applications as they are received, decisions may be made at any time if a suitable candidate is identified. UK-Med is committed to safeguarding of our personnel and beneficiaries and has a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation and abuse. We conduct thorough vetting before any appointment is confirmed. UK-Med is committed to the principles of diversity, equality, and inclusion. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive environment where employees feel respected and supported to be able to fulfil their potential.
item.dc:creator: UK-Med

item.title: Data Management Officer
item.description: About Scotland's Charity Air Ambulance Scotland’s Charity Air Ambulance (SCAA) exists so nobody in Scotland suffers or dies because medical help cannot get there in time. People can get sick or have accidents anywhere and anytime. But in Scotland there are places where urgent medical help cannot reach people. Or help gets there too late. And when lives are at risk every minute matters. As a charity we rely on donations from the Scottish public, companies and communities to ensure that urgent medical help gets to the patient when it is needed, wherever they are and at whatever time of day. The Role We are looking for a skilled and proactive Data Management Officer to join the charity’s Data and Insights Function. You will be joining the charity at a time of significant opportunity as we continue to strengthen our approach to data, insight and supporter engagement. The Data Management Officer will mainly be responsible for managing and developing our Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system and supporter data. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced CRM and data professional who enjoys hands-on responsibility for systems, process improvement and data management, and enabling colleagues to deliver exceptional fundraising, marketing and supporter engagement activity. Working closely with teams across the charity, you will ensure our CRM remains effective, compliant and fit for purpose while helping us better understand and engage our supporters. Your work will directly contribute to our ability to raise funds and support our life-saving mission. This role can be offered on a fully remote basis, with the option to work from Perth Airport, where SCAA headquarters are located or our Aberdeen base at Aberdeen Airport, if preferred. Occasional travel to our Perth base will be required for the successful candidate. SCAA supports flexible and hybrid working arrangements—our current approach typically includes two office days per week for those working on a hybrid basis. The usual hours and days of work will be Monday to Friday, 9am—5pm. About You Essential Proven experience managing CRM systems in a charity or fundraising context and being comfortable working with large datasets. Experience with data segmentation, ETL processes, transformation and import / export processes. Strong understanding of data protection legislation (e.g. GDPR). Understanding of Gift Aid regulations and charity fundraising compliance. Confident using query tools and an understanding of query-based data extraction. Strong IT skills with competency using the MS Office suite and Excel in particular. Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work collaboratively across teams and support non-technical colleagues. Ability to analyse and translate data into clear findings for campaigns and reporting, including donor value analysis. Our Benefits Pension: 12% employer’s & 5% employee’s contribution (after 3 months’ service) Annual Leave: 36 days (incl. public holidays) + an extra day for your birthday (and additional days with long service) Death in Service benefit: 4 times annual salary Optional Private Medical Insurance plan and Cashplan Employee Assistance Programme Enhanced Maternity/Adoption/Paternity Pay Access to Blue Light Card Learning and Development Opportunities Selection Process Interviews will take place at our base at Perth Airport in Scone, or remotely, during the weeks commencing the 24th or 31st August 2026. How to apply Please refer to the full job pack on our website. Application deadline is 5pm on Sunday 16th August 2026.
